summary.text: A 75-year-old African-American woman with diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, four prior cerebrovascular accidents with mild right sided residual weakness and a repaired ventral hernia, with no prior smoking, alcohol or illicit drug use, presented with shortness of breath, rhinorrhea and productive cough. She tested positive for influenza A and was started on oseltamivir.

On her second hospital day she had mild retrosternal chest pain, troponin I elevation up to 0.3 ng/mL and an unchanged EKG showing RBBB, and received aspirin, clopidogrel, heparin drip, diltiazem and atorvastatin as treatment for a NSTEMI. A coronary angiogram showed only minor luminal irregularities. Nasopharyngolaryngoscopy for progressive dysphonia showed inflammatory laryngeal changes, and intramuscular dexamethasone 10 mg Q8 hours was then started.

She then had severe retrosternal chest pain with blood pressure 90/65 mmHg, an unremarkable cardiovascular examination and EKG ST elevation in leads V2 to V5. Bedside echocardiography showed an EF of 30-35% with regional wall motion abnormalities, unlike the normal pre-MI study. Angiography showed a filling defect, likely a thrombus, occluding the mid LAD; a drug eluting stent was deployed with TIMI III flow and eptifibatide was started.

Chest pain resolved shortly after the intervention and the EKG returned to baseline. Blood work showed a platelet count of 461 k/cumm, elevated high sensitivity CRP, mildly elevated homocysteine and increased factor VIII, factor XI and thrombin antithrombin complex, with normal factor VII, fibrinogen, protein C and S, and negative cardiolipin antibody, JAK2 V617F and Factor V Leiden testing.
